chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Umar, from Al-Hajj, from Dawud ibn Abi Yazeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

A man said, 'I have acquired some wealth, and I feared for my soul regarding it. If I were to find its owner, I would hand it over to him and be rid of it.' So Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him, 'By Allah, if you were to find him, would you hand it over to him?' He said, 'Yes, by Allah.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Then it is I, by Allah, there is no other owner for it but me.' He said, 'So he made him swear an oath that he would hand it over to whomever he commanded him to.' So he swore an oath. He (peace be upon him) said, 'Go and distribute it among your brethren, and for you is security from what you feared from it.' He said, 'So I distributed it among my brethren.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for found wealth when the owner is unknown?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) employs a psychological test to verify the finder's sincerity regarding unknown wealth, ultimately declaring himself the owner to grant the finder security (*aman*) from the spiritual and material risks of hoarding. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Imam's authority to purify property and distribute it as charity, transforming a potential burden into a means of spiritual purification for the finder. The incident underscores the practical application of *mal al-malfuf* (found wrapped property) jurisprudence, where the Imam's declaration serves as the definitive mechanism for resolving ownership ambiguity.
